mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week reduction in negative RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained return to workplaces, evidenced by WORKPLACES mobility remaining less negative than -10% for two consecutive weeks, signifies increased daily commuting and out-of-home presence, which directly translates to higher retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility is less negative than -10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, even when WORKPLACES mobility consistently stays above -10% for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent increase in TRANSIT mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a shift in daily routines where people are spending less time at home and utilizing public transport more, leading to increased opportunities for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite both TRANSIT mobility increasing and RESIDENTIAL mobility decreasing over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, the significant rebound in PARKS mobility from a recent low indicates renewed public confidence in outdoor activities and social interaction, which typically precedes or coincides with increased retail and recreation engagement over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility shows a week-on-week increase of more than 5 points after a decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase, even when PARKS mobility rebounds significantly in a reopening phase.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent downward trend in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks indicates that people are spending progressively less time at home, freeing up time and opportunity for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite a continued downward trend in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility exceeds 25% and shows a week-on-week increase, it signals a high baseline level of essential movement and public activity, creating a supportive environment for increased discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility exceeds 25% and shows a week-on-week increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility exceeding 25% and increasing week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and sustained increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a robust return to daily commuting and work routines, which directly drives increased footfall in retail and recreation areas, particularly during weekdays, over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility showing consistent increases.

mechanism_narrative: A combined rebound in PARKS mobility and sustained high levels of GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggest a general increase in public comfort and willingness to engage in out-of-home activities, both essential and recreational, which will positively impact retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite PARKS mobility rebounding and GROCERY_PHARM mobility remaining high.
